images.title: Halve, then halve again
images.purpose: Show repeated angle bisection: a right angle halved to 45°, and one 45° part halved again to 22.5°.
images.composition: One vertex O at the lower left; a right angle opening up and to the right, filling about half the frame; the two bisectors fanning between the arms.
exact_structure: A vertex O at the lower left, labelled O, with one dark horizontal arm to the right and one dark vertical arm upwards, and a small square right angle mark at O.
A teal (#0072B2) ray from O at 45° to the horizontal arm, bisecting the right angle.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) ray from O at 22.5° to the horizontal arm, bisecting the lower 45° part.
One large grey (#6B7280) arc centred at O crossing the horizontal arm, the teal ray and the vertical arm.

Two short grey (#6B7280) crossing arcs on the teal ray (centred where the large arc meets the two arms) and two short grey (#6B7280) crossing arcs on the reddish purple ray (centred where the large arc meets the horizontal arm and the teal ray); 4 short arcs in all.
Label 45° inside the angle between the teal ray and the vertical arm; label 22.5° inside the angle between the horizontal arm and the reddish purple ray; label 90° just outside the right angle mark.
One short caption line at the bottom of the frame.
rejection: the reddish purple ray not exactly halfway between the horizontal arm and the teal ray
the 22.5° label placed in the wrong wedge, or any angle value other than 90°, 45° and 22.5°
other than 4 short crossing arcs, or the angle at O not a right angle
images.takeaway: Each bisection halves the angle exactly, so 90° gives 45° and then 22.5°.
images.description: A right angle at O with a teal 45° bisector and a reddish purple ray halving the lower part again into 22.5°, with grey construction arcs.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Trace the two bisections in order, then ask which other angles repeated halving can reach.

image_decisions.why: Repeated halving is the method this practice builds on, and one picture of two bisections shows it at a glance.
